title: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)

sections.label: PDO cases and small law firms
sections.summary: MP asks for an update on PDO cases, a review of means testing criteria, and help for small law firms to win international work and consolidate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister provide an update on the number of cases the PDO has taken up to date, as well as whether there would be a review of the means testing criteria, seeing as about half of rejected applications were because the applicants did not meet the prescribed means criteria?

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Domestically, we have over 1,000 law firms, with over 80% being small law firms with five or less lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These firms, however, contribute to only about 40% of value-add.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister elaborate on what the Ministry is doing to help small law firms get a firmer bite of the pie of the international work that is coming into Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And second, would the Ministry consider encouraging consolidation in the industry, including through incentives, to help small law firms come together to form larger practices that are more full service and that would place them better to seize opportunities in the market?

sections.label: PDO means threshold and applications
sections.summary: When PDO was established, criminal defence aid was widened by raising the means threshold from the 25th to the 35th percentile, and about 1,700 applications were received as of December 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: When PDO was established, criminal defence aid was made available to more people, by raising the means threshold from the 25th to the 35th percentile of resident households based on per capita household income and allowing aid for most non-capital criminal offences, with some exceptions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As of December 2023, we have received about 1,700 applications.

sections.label: PDO Public Defenders and accused
sections.summary: As of December 2023, PDO had 16 Public Defenders who represented more than 440 accused in Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As of December 2023, PDO has a team of 16 Public Defenders and they represented more than 440 accused in Court.

sections.label: Court sentence imposed
sections.summary: The Court eventually gave a sentence of six weeks' imprisonment with a fine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Eventually, the Court gave a sentence of six weeks’ imprisonment with a fine.

sections.label: LAB recovers daughter's monies
sections.summary: LAB helped her secure a Court order for her daughter to return all her monies, with interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: LAB helped her to secure a Court order for her daughter to return all her monies, with interest.

sections.label: Conditional fee agreements in Singapore
sections.summary: CFAs can help litigants who do not qualify for legal aid but cannot pay full litigation costs, and Singapore has permitted them in arbitration, certain Singapore International Commercial Court proceedings, and related court and mediation proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: CFAs have the potential to help people access justice faster, easier when they do not qualify for legal aid, but also find it challenging to pay the full costs of litigation in the Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: CFAs can help litigants, who are unable to fork out full legal fees at the outset, by providing an additional funding option, to pursue their claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: However, it is not an unvarnished benefit, if you look at the examples in other countries, which is why we have been and we continue to be careful about it, because you have got to weigh against these possible benefits, some well-known potential negative consequences of CFAs, and these are visible in other places.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So far, in Singapore, we have permitted CFAs in arbitration proceedings, certain proceedings in the Singapore International Commercial Court, and court and mediation proceedings, which are related to these proceedings where CFAs have been allowed.

sections.label: Divorce cases past year
sections.summary: There were about 6,220 divorce cases in the past year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you take the past year, there were a total of about 6,220 divorce cases.

sections.label: Simplified track resolution rate
sections.summary: Of simplified track cases, 4,150, or 94%, were resolved within six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Of those cases that go on the simplified track, the 4,150, 94% were resolved within six months.

sections.label: Court monitors payments
sections.summary: The Court monitors payments typically for around six months, and failure to pay can lead to imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Court will monitor payments, typically for around six months and failure to pay can lead to imprisonment.

sections.label: Technical amendments and MEP phasing
sections.summary: Some technical amendments commenced in January, with the MEP targeted to be operationalised in phases from the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Some of the technical amendments were commenced in January this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In particular, we are targeting to operationalise the MEP in phases, starting from the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: MinLaw works closely with MSF and FJC to improve the family justice system.

sections.label: Aim of family justice
sections.summary: The aim remains to reduce acrimony, preserve relationships and protect children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The aim remains pretty much the same: reduce acrimony, preserve relationships and protect children.

sections.label: Legal services sector growth
sections.summary: Legal services nominal value-added rose over 25% from $2.36 billion in 2018 to $2.98 billion in 2023, and exports rose nearly 35%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The nominal value-added of our legal services sector increased by more than 25%, from $2.36 billion in 2018 to $2.98 billion in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our exports of legal services have also increased by nearly 35%, from $1.04 billion in 2018 to $1.40 billion in 2023.

sections.label: SICC caseload and innovation ranking
sections.summary: SICC caseload rose about 30% last year, and Singapore ranked top in Asia and fifth globally in the 2023 Global Innovation Index.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) saw an increased caseload as well last year, up by about 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our IP regime and innovation environment are also internationally recognised.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We were ranked top in Asia and fifth in the world in the 2023 Global Innovation Index.

sections.label: Convention signatories and parties
sections.summary: There are currently 56 signatories and, as of today, 14 Parties, including Sri Lanka, which ratified two days ago.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Currently, there are 56 signatories and, as of today, 14 Parties, including Sri Lanka, who just ratified the Convention two days ago.

sections.label: Singapore-Shanghai lawyers exchange programme
sections.summary: Singapore and the Law Society introduced the Singapore-Shanghai Lawyers Exchange Programme last year, hosting 10 Shanghai lawyers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: One of the key markets, to give you an example, is China.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We introduced the Singapore-Shanghai Lawyers Exchange Programme together with the Law Society last year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our firms in Singapore hosted the inaugural batch of 10 Shanghai lawyers.

sections.label: Singapore lawyers to Shanghai
sections.summary: Later this year, Singapore lawyers will be sent to Shanghai on the return leg of the exchange programme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Later this year, we will be sending our Singapore lawyers to Shanghai on the return leg of the exchange programme.

sections.label: Longer practice training period
sections.summary: A key recommendation to lengthen the practice training period from six months to one year will be implemented this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: One key recommendation – to lengthen the practice training period from six months to one year – will be implemented this year.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up for legal professionals
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, for all Singaporeans aged 40 and above, will also apply to legal professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, which is applicable to all Singaporeans aged 40 and above, this programme will also apply to legal professionals.

sections.label: Legal Industry Digital Plan
sections.summary: MinLaw and IMDA introduced the Legal Industry Digital Plan in October 2023, identifying tools to automate knowledge work.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In October 2023, MinLaw and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) introduced the Legal Industry Digital Plan (IDP), and as part of the Legal IDP, we identified tools that will help automate knowledge work.

sections.label: Patent and trademark filings
sections.summary: Singapore's patent filings grew by 40% and trademark filings by 35% over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our patent filings grew by 40% and our trademark filings grew by 35% over the last decade.

sections.label: Singapore IP Strategy 2030
sections.summary: MinLaw, MOF and MTI launched the Singapore IP Strategy or SIPS 2030 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MinLaw, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) therefore launched the Singapore IP Strategy or SIPS 2030 in 2021.

sections.label: IPOS launched IP Ready
sections.summary: In September last year, IPOS launched IP Ready.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In September last year, IPOS launched IP Ready.

sections.label: Intangibles Disclosure Framework
sections.summary: Last September, the Intangibles Disclosure Framework was launched to help businesses disclose their IA systematically and consistently.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Last September, we launched the Intangibles Disclosure Framework, which helps businesses disclose their IA in a systematic and consistent manner.

sections.label: Community Mediation Centre mediators
sections.summary: The Community Mediation Centre increased volunteer mediators by 15% over the past year in anticipation of increasing cases, given mandated mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Community Mediation Centre (CMC) has, therefore, increased the number of volunteer mediators by 15% over the past year, in anticipation of such increasing cases, given that we are mandating mediation.

sections.label: Satellite centres and mandated mediation
sections.summary: Satellite centres grew from six to 10, with plans for more, and mediation will be mandated in appropriate cases.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the past year, we have grown the number of satellite centres from six to 10 and have plans to add more in the neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To drive more cases towards an early and amicable settlement, we will, therefore, mandate mediation in appropriate cases.

sections.label: Abatement orders for nuisance
sections.summary: A team satisfied of persistent nuisance or egregious conduct can issue an abatement order to stop the nuisance pending mediation or CDRT adjudication.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If this team is satisfied that there is evidence of persistent nuisance or otherwise egregious conduct, it can also issue an abatement order, which is a direction for the particular nuisance to stop, pending a mediation or a CDRT adjudication.

sections.label: CDRT interim orders in serious cases
sections.summary: In serious cases, the CDRT will be empowered to make interim orders on an expedited basis and a lower threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, in serious cases, the CDRT will be empowered to make interim orders on an expedited basis and based on a lower threshold.

sections.label: SLA state properties for new uses
sections.summary: SLA innovations include former St Andrew's Mission Hospital becoming a creative lifestyle space, and Hindoo Road and Evans Road properties for co-living.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A few examples of SLA’s innovations and curation of new uses include: the former St Andrew’s Mission Hospital in Tanjong Pagar which will be transformed into a creative lifestyle space.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: SLA has also made available state properties such as 79 to 95 Hindoo Road and 26 Evans Road to meet the emergent demand for co-living spaces.

sections.label: The Foundry at Prinsep Link
sections.summary: The Foundry at 11 Prinsep Link was the former Elections Department office building.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: One example is The Foundry at 11 Prinsep Link, which was the former Elections Department office building.

sections.label: Former Kampong Chai Chee community centre
sections.summary: A tender was launched for the former Kampong Chai Chee community centre to create space for social activities and interaction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Another new site is the former Kampong Chai Chee community centre.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have launched a tender to create a new space for social activities and interaction among diverse communities.

sections.label: State property occupancy rate
sections.summary: In financial year 2022, the occupancy rate for all usable state properties was 99%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In financial year 2022, the occupancy rate for all usable state properties was 99%.

sections.label: SLA revenue and geospatial plan
sections.summary: SLA's state property revenue exceeds maintenance costs, and SLA will launch the refreshed Singapore Geospatial Master Plan in March.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Today, overall, the total revenue collected by SLA from state properties significantly exceeds the total maintenance cost incurred.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: On the issue of building local capability in geospatial data, SLA will be launching the refreshed Singapore Geospatial Master Plan in March this year.

sections.label: Barrier-free routes in OneMap
sections.summary: Barrier-free routes in OneMap were piloted with over 100 wheelchair users across about 1,100 kilometres in nine planning areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: One initiative is the introduction of barrier-free routes in OneMap.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: These routes have been piloted with more than 100 wheelchair users, covering about 1,100 kilometres across nine planning areas, including Gardens by the Bay and the Orchard Road precinct.

sections.label: National aerial mapping exercise
sections.summary: SLA will conduct the third national aerial mapping exercise in March to capture and update Singapore in 3D.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: SLA will conduct the third national aerial mapping exercise to capture and update Singapore in 3D in March this year.

sections.label: PCHI thresholds for legal aid
sections.summary: PCHI thresholds will increase for civil legal aid from $950 to $1,050 and for criminal defence aid from $1,500 to $1,650.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The PCHI thresholds will be increased for civil legal aid from $950 to $1,050, and for criminal defence aid from $1,500 to $1,650.

sections.label: eBantu for nafkah claims
sections.summary: eBantu lets applicants estimate nafkah iddah and mutaah claims and uses guided questions to help fill in originating documents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Applicants can use eBantu to get an estimate of the nafkah iddah and mutaah claimable. eBantu also uses a series of guided questions to help the applicant fill in originating documents.

sections.label: Probate and Family Justice Rules
sections.summary: MinLaw targets introducing a Bill this year, and the FJC launched a Probate e-Service in 2023 and intends to roll out revamped Family Justice Rules.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MinLaw has made good progress on refining its proposals, having sought inputs from various stakeholders in the past year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We target to introduce the Bill later this year and will provide details in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The FJC launched its Probate e-Service in 2023 for straightforward probate applications where the estate is not more than $2 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Separately, the FJC also intends to roll out its revamped Family Justice Rules later this year, which will simplify and streamline the rules on family proceedings, including probate and intestacy proceedings.

sections.label: MinLaw Committee of Supply thrusts
sections.summary: MinLaw will in 2024 increase access to justice, strengthen Singapore as a legal services hub, and optimise state assets using geospatial technology.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To round off the MinLaw Committee of Supply (COS), let me highlight the key thrusts of our work.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We will in 2024 strive to increase access to justice for more in the community, especially the most vulnerable; strengthen Singapore's position as a leading international legal services hub and seize new opportunities; and finally, optimise our state assets and leverage geospatial technology to support the economy and serve the community.

sections.label: Litigant-in-person Courts touchpoint
sections.summary: For a litigant-in-person, the primary touchpoint will be the Courts, because the MEOs report to the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For a litigant-in-person, the primary touchpoint will be the Courts, because the MEOs report to the Court and that is where he will get the information.

sections.label: Conference and Family Justice Reform Act
sections.summary: Last year a major conference was held, with SG Her Empowerment partnering the Ministry, and the Family Justice Reform Act was widely discussed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, last year, there was a major conference on these developments and the non-government organisation SG Her Empowerment, or SHE, partnered the Ministry in having the conference, and the Family Justice Reform Act was widely discussed.

sections.label: PDO means testing and CLAS
sections.summary: Cases not qualifying through PDO means testing go to CLAS, which can act for non-citizens whereas PDO only acts for citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think those questions are best addressed to the Law Society.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But broadly, what the Member can assume that those cases that do not qualify through the means testing of PDO, go to CLAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: CLAS, for example, has the power to act for non-citizens, whereas PDO will only act for citizens.

sections.label: Taking back enhancement suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker says it would be a useful endeavour and they will take it back to see how best to enhance it further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Indeed, I think that would be a useful endeavour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will take this back and see how best we can enhance this further.

sections.label: Intangible asset valuation standards work
sections.summary: Three Ministries are working with industry professionals to agree on standards for valuing intangible assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Indeed, also Mr Christopher de Souza is right that valuing it, how you do valuation, what standards, what parameters you look at, what are some of the features of an intangible asset that ought to go into valuation – all that has to be looked at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, as I mentioned in my speech earlier, we are working with MOF and MTI, three Ministries coming together, to look at the landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If you do not have that across different jurisdictions, different markets, it is going to be very hard for something to be marketed, to be monetised or even if you want to use it to raise money, raise capital or provide security, it is going to be difficult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, the first thing that we have got to do is to agree on a set of standards and that is what we are working on now, working with leading industry professionals, not just in Singapore, but elsewhere in other jurisdictions, coming together.

sections.label: Trainee pay and support
sections.summary: Trainee pay is left to firms, while Law Society support covers leave days and mentoring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Yes, we do not think we should prescribe how much each trainee will be paid across this duration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is something that they can work out with the firms at which they are training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But we can and we have worked with Law Society to see what additional support can be given and whether it is in terms of leave days or indeed the mentoring scheme that Law Society has put in place.

sections.label: Black and white bungalow income costs
sections.summary: A question asks for total rental income and maintenance cost attributable to black and white bungalows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can I specifically ask for the total rental income and total maintenance cost attributable to the black and white bungalows?

sections.label: SLA rental subsidies for arts tenants
sections.summary: A clarification asks whether SLA presently provides no rental subsidies to artist or arts group tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My first clarification, if I understand the Senior Parliamentary Secretary correctly, is it the case that presently, no rental subsidies are provided by SLA to tenants that are either artists or arts groups?

sections.label: Agencies administer rental subsidies
sections.summary: Rental subsidies are administered and managed by the agencies overseeing that sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The rental subsidies are administered and managed by the agencies that are overseeing that sector.

sections.label: NAC manages arts spaces centrally
sections.summary: Arts spaces are managed centrally by NAC, which subvents through its Arts Housing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For the arts spaces, they are managed centrally by the agencies, in this case, the National Arts Council (NAC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As the Member knows, NAC has the Arts Housing Scheme over different versions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I will not go into detail now, but depending on the size of the company, the nature of the artist, NAC has a programme where it subvents at the central level.

sections.label: black and white bungalow information
sections.summary: A Member says the Ministry has not shared total income, maintenance cost and land area of black and white bungalows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: For example, up to today I do not think the Ministry has shared what is the total income derived and what is the total maintenance cost spent on managing the black and white bungalows, and what is the total land area occupied by the black and white bungalows and all that.

sections.label: land demand outstrips supply
sections.summary: The speaker notes the point and says demand for land in Singapore mostly outstrips supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I hope you will say that again at the MCCY COS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But the point is noted and, in most cases, the demand, especially for land in Singapore, does outstrip the supply.

sections.label: Kampong Java arts space
sections.summary: Kampong Java, obtained by NAC with SLA, will open this year as an artist-run space for artists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ms Usha might know that later this year, Kampong Java will be open.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Kampong Java is a space that NAC worked with SLA to obtain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is a new space altogether, meant for artists and will be artist-run so that artists themselves will decide how to run the space, what kind of exhibitions to hold there, which arts companies will come in and use the spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, it is our way also of working with the community to expand the number of spaces in tandem with the growing interest that arts companies have shown.

sections.label: EIU business environment ranking
sections.summary: For the 15th consecutive year the EIU ranked Singapore as the world's leading business environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Last year, for the 15th consecutive year, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) ranked Singapore as the world's leading business environment citing our technological readiness, infrastructure, connectivity and regulatory environment as reasons, amongst others.

sections.label: Hague Judgments Convention accession
sections.summary: A Member recommends Singapore consider the merits of acceding to the 2019 Hague Judgments Convention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, I recommend that Singapore consider the merits of acceding to the 2019 Hague Judgments Convention.

sections.label: indentures exclusion from Electronic Transactions Act
sections.summary: A Member suggests removing indentures from the Electronic Transactions Act 2010 exclusion list sooner rather than later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This does not appear to square with Singapore's position as a leading business and financial hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would respectfully suggest the time has come to remove indentures from the exclusion list of documents that are not subject to the Electronic Transactions Act 2010 sooner rather than later.

sections.label: Public Defender's Office setup
sections.summary: The Public Defender's Office was set up in 2022, described as an epochal moment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The set up of the Public Defender's Office in 2022 was an epochal moment.

sections.label: 1961 Wills Convention accession
sections.summary: The viability of Singapore acceding to the 1961 Wills Convention, with 42 contracting parties including China, is being considered.

sentences.text: One connected point, having regard to the fact that Singaporeans have become increasingly affluent over the years and may hold property in other jurisdictions, is the viability of Singapore acceding to the 1961 Wills Convention, which has 42 contracting parties at this point, including China, being considered.

sections.label: Government rent from state properties
sections.summary: The 2022 Government Financial Statement states the Government received $1.4 billion in rent, presumably from 2,600 SLA-managed state properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For 2022, it is stated in the Government Financial Statement that the Government received $1.4 billion in rent, presumably from the 2,600 state properties managed by SLA, which include about 600 black and white bungalows.

sections.label: 26 Ridout Road vacancy
sections.summary: No. 26 Ridout Road was vacant and in very bad condition for over four years before being rented out.

sentences.text: For example, No. 26 Ridout Road was vacant and in a very bad condition for more than four years before it was rented out.

sentences.text: In August last year, I asked a Parliamentary Question about the occupancy rate and median vacancy period of black and white bungalows, but these specific numbers were not revealed.

sections.label: SLA cost-benefit analysis urged
sections.summary: PSP urges SLA to conduct a cost-benefit analysis on whether higher rents justify modernising black and white bungalows with amenities like air conditioning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP urges SLA to conduct a cost-benefit analysis to determine whether higher rents will make it worthwhile for SLA to modernise black and white bungalows with amenities like air conditioning, like what other private landlords do.

sections.label: SLA land parcels development review
sections.summary: SLA should review whether developing land parcels per the URA Master Plan and investing proceeds in Past Reserves makes better economic sense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Where appropriate, SLA should review whether it would make better economic sense to develop these land parcels in line with the URA Master Plan and invest the land sales proceeds as part of the Past Reserves.

sections.label: SLA properties for arts groups
sections.summary: MinLaw is asked about plans for longer-term use of SLA-managed properties by arts groups and the factors in lease evaluations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry of Law clarify if there are any plans underway for more SLA-managed properties to be put to longer-term use by arts groups; and if so, whether they will be offered subsidised rental rates?

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Minister K Shanmugan had mentioned that a potential extension of lease terms for the Pearl's Hill Terrace tenants would depend on an assessment by the relevant agencies; and that these agencies would look at "their value and the service they provide to the community." Would the Ministry be able to provide more specific detail on the kinds of factors that will be taken into consideration when such an evaluation is made?

sections.label: Enforcement of civil judgments review
sections.summary: MinLaw is asked to review enforcement of civil judgments to make it more effective, efficient, economical and simpler.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The enforcement process and cost of doing so often turns many of them away and often leave them high and dry, as they hold back from incurring even more cost of enforcement for their judgment debt or order of court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I therefore submit that MinLaw review this space of the enforcement of civil judgments to make it more effective, efficient, economical and simpler.

sections.label: Criminal justice system update
sections.summary: MinLaw is asked for an update on developments to enhance Singapore's criminal justice system, including criminal procedure and sentencing frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In the same vein, there has been notable reviews and updates to our criminal justice system in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am therefore asking MinLaw for an update on the developments to further enhance and improve our criminal justice system in Singapore, which includes amongst others, criminal procedure and sentencing frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When they need to access legal information, they face difficulties because most of the legal information provided by Government agencies is written in English.

sections.label: Judgment debtor powers changes
sections.summary: Rahayu Mahzam indicated potential changes: giving the Court more powers to identify non-compliant judgment debtors' assets and new powers to deter non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the Committee of Supply debates in 2023, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam indicated that potential changes being considered were: one, giving the Court more powers to identify the assets and means of a non-compliant judgment debtor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Second, to introduce new powers to deter and punish non-compliance with Court orders.

sections.label: Family Justice Reform recommendations
sections.summary: The Committee's July 2014 report made key recommendations, many adopted in the Family Justice Reform Act passed in May 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In its report that was prepared following consultations with the public and key stakeholders and released in July 2014, the Committee made several key recommendations – many of which were laudably adopted in the Family Justice Reform Act passed by MinLaw and Ministry of Social Development and Family in May 2023.

sections.label: Public Defender's Office introduction
sections.summary: MinLaw introduced the Public Defender's Office in December 2022 as a fully funded scheme, helping around 303 cases in Court by September last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A milestone achieved was MinLaw's introduction of the Public Defender's Office (PDO) in December 2022 – as a fully funded scheme offering vulnerable residents legal assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that since its founding till September last year, the PDO had helped around 303 cases in Court.

sections.label: Neighbour noise disputes high
sections.summary: Neighbour disputes over noise remained high at over 2,000 per month last year, five times pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Notably, the number of neighbour disputes over noise remains high – at over 2,000 per month last year, five times pre-COVID-19 levels.

sections.label: Community Mediation Centre resolution rate
sections.summary: Cases mediated by the Community Mediation Centre continue to see a high-resolution rate at 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: A good outcome is that cases mediated by the Community Mediation Centre (CMC) continues to see a high-resolution rate at 80%.

sections.label: Enhancing community dispute management framework
sections.summary: MinLaw committed to creating a special unit for serious noise disputes and making mediation mandatory with penalties for non-attendance and non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: At last year's Committee of Supply, MinLaw committed to enhancing the community dispute management framework by: one, creating a special unit to deal with the more serious noise disputes; and two, making mediation mandatory, with penalties for non-attendance and non-compliance to orders.

sections.label: Feedback on mediation being laborious
sections.summary: Residents have given feedback that mediation or the CDRT is laborious and time-consuming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Over the years, one of the feedback that we have received from residents is that mediation or the CDRT is laborious and time-consuming.

sections.label: IP applications growth and support
sections.summary: Between 2015 and 2020, Singapore-based pattern applications grew 21% and trademark applications rose 51%, prompting a call for an update on IAIP resource accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Chairman, between 2015 and 2020, the number of Singapore-based pattern applications grew 21%, while the corresponding number of trademark applications rose by 51%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is hence important to support businesses and securing their intangible assets and intellectual property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, I commend the Singapore IP Strategy 2030 which has a strong focus on supporting enterprises on this front.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could we have an update on the results of the whole- of-Government touch points to make IAIP resources more accessible, including the rollout of training courses on IAIP and the provision of consultation services with IAIP advisors?

sections.label: SIAC case filings figures
sections.summary: SIAC received 357 new case filings in 2022, with 332 in the first quarter of 2023 and 88% of 2022 cases international.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Chairman, in 2022, SIAC received 357 new case filings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Although the full figures for 2023 has not yet been released, just in the first quarter of 2023, new case filings at SIAC were at a historical high, with 332 new cases filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In 2022, 88% of new cases filed at SIAC were international in nature.

sections.label: Strengthening Singapore legal hub
sections.summary: The question asks what MinLaw is doing to strengthen Singapore's legal and dispute resolution hub status, including technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: What is MinLaw doing to strengthen Singapore's leading legal and dispute resolution hub status, including supporting the legal profession and harnessing technology, for instance data analytics and Generative AI?
